events.outcome: Current STC personal prepaid terms document 180-day SIM validity from paid activity, while a still-live STC recharge page says 360 days; non-citizen final-departure/ID-expiry cancellation remains a structural blocker.

data.acquisitionSummary: Current STC Sawa prepaid is locally sold through STC channels; non-citizen continuity depends on valid Saudi identity/legal status.

keep.action: Any paid activity can extend prepaid validity, but current STC pages conflict on whether the SIM ceiling is 180 or 360 days. Minimum documented recharge via postpaid-to-Sawa is SAR15; do not treat this as a proven annual keep minimum.

data.chinaActivation: Local Saudi activation/identity status required; not a remote China activation route.
data.kyc: STC general terms permit cancellation after ID validity expires or final departure from Saudi Arabia for a non-citizen.
data.payment: mystc/recharge cards and other STC channels; one documented recharge channel has SAR15 minimum.
data.roamingSms: STC offers roaming generally, but long-term OTP utility after non-citizen final departure is not a stable use case.
data.refund: remaining balance can be depleted/transferred in some disconnection/operator-transfer cases; not fully reconciled.
data.holdReason: Provider pages conflict on 180 vs 360-day SIM retention, and STC may cancel a non-citizen line after final departure or ID expiry.
data.tariffSummary: Paid activity extends Sawa validity; current first-party pages conflict on 180 vs 360 days and non-citizen legal-status termination is material.
guideSteps: Do not model SAR15 as a guaranteed annual keep-alive floor.
Do not recommend for nonresident long-term OTP while final-departure cancellation remains in STC terms.
